sourceStandard.lexicalComparison: James Strong original dictionaries, accessed through attributed pinned digital transcription
sourceStandard.uncertainty: Conflicts and unsupported derivations remain explicitly unresolved
sourceStandard.foundationalDecisions: Ask the owner explicitly and wait for an answer before implementation; do not choose an assumed default.

sources.attribution: James Strong, Hebrew and Greek dictionaries; JSON transcription copyright Open Scriptures, CC-BY-SA (source headers retained unchanged; license version not specified in headers).

webster.edition: Noah Webster, American Dictionary of the English Language (1828)
webster.excerpt: To notice; to take particular observation of.
webster.scope: English sense only; no claim of a Webster 1828 Shadrach entry or name etymology.

meta.coverageNote: Every entry compared against the pinned lexical records; unresolved entries remain unresolved. Digital transcription, not a facsimile verification of every original printed page.
meta.license: Review annotations: CC BY-SA; OpenScriptures source excerpts retain their original CC-BY-SA headers and attribution. Original Strong dictionary text is public domain; Hitchcock digital source: CC BY 4.0.

entries.name: Aaron
entries.note: Strong H175 explicitly gives uncertain derivation; Hitchcock's three meanings are historical proposals, not established by this comparison.
hitchcock: a teacher; lofty; mountain of strength

entries.name: Abaddon
entries.note: Revelation 9:11 explicitly gives the Greek equivalent Apollyon; Strong G3 calls Abaddon a destroying angel. The title identifies the angel of the bottomless pit. [Strong G3](https://biblehub.com/greek/3.htm).

entries.name: Abagtha
entries.note: H5 identifies the eunuch in Esther 1:10 but supplies no wine-press etymology.

entries.name: Abana
entries.note: H71 proposes stony only tentatively; building is not supplied as the name meaning.

strongs.derivation: perhaps feminine of H68 (אֶבֶן); stony;  Compare H549 (אֲמָנָה).

entries.name: Abarim
entries.note: Strong H5682 gives regions beyond and the KJV rendering passages. Hitchcock's passengers is not established as the place-name's sense. [Strong H5682](https://biblehub.com/hebrew/5682.htm).

entries.name: Abba
entries.note: G5 is a form of address to the Father, not a personal proper name; see Mark 14:36.

identity.text: An address followed by Father in each of its three KJV occurrences. These passages do not introduce a person named Abba.

entries.name: Abda
entries.note: H5653 derives the name from work/service. Two Israelites share this spelling; the gloss does not identify which.

strongs.strongs_def: Abda, the name of two Israelites

entries.name: Abdeel
entries.note: H5655 derives Abdeel from serving and God; the vapor/cloud reading is a conflicting historical etymology. [Strong H5655](https://biblehub.com/hebrew/5655.htm).
hitchcock: a vapor; a cloud of God

strongs.derivation: from H5647 (עָבַד) and H410 (אֵל); serving God;

entries.name: Abdi
entries.note: H5660 gives serviceable, rather than the possessive my servant; the spelling covers multiple Israelites.

strongs.strongs_def: Abdi, the name of two Israelites

entries.name: Abdiel
entries.note: H5661 supplies this derivation; the initial exact-candidate index omitted the name.

strongs.derivation: from H5650 (עֶבֶד) and H410 (אֵל); servant of God;

entries.name: Abdon
entries.note: H5658 supplies servitude; servant is related, but cloud of judgment is unsupported. The spelling denotes both a town (Joshua 21:30) and several men (Judges 12:13; 1 Chronicles 8:23). [Strong H5658](https://biblehub.com/hebrew/5658.htm).

strongs.strongs_def: Abdon, the name of a place in Palestine and of four Israelites

entries.name: Abednego
entries.note: H5664/H5665 identify Azariah under his Babylonian name; servant of light is not established by these entries. The input lacks hyphenated KJV references; see Daniel 1:7.

strongs.strongs_def: Abed-Nego, the Babylonian name of one of Daniel's companions

identity.text: Azariah, given the Babylonian name Abed-nego. With Hananiah and Mishael, he refused to worship the golden image. God delivered the three from the furnace.

entries.name: Abel
entries.displayMeaning: Person: vanity or transitoriness; place: meadow
entries.note: H1893/H1892 concern Adam's son; H59 concerns places. Do not merge these as one derivation. Mourning is not H59's proposed meaning.

strongs.strongs_def: Abel, the name of two places in Palestine.

entries.name: Abel-beth-maachah
entries.note: H62 gives meadow of Beth-maakah, differing from Hitchcock's mourning. Treat as a place-name. [Strong H62](https://biblehub.com/hebrew/62.htm).
hitchcock: mourning to the house of Maachah

strongs.derivation: from H58 (אָבֵל) and H1004 (בַּיִת) and H4601 (מַעֲכָה); meadow of Beth-Maakah;
strongs.strongs_def: Abel of Beth-maakah, a place in Palestine

entries.name: Abel-maim
entries.note: H66 gives meadow of water, whereas Hitchcock gives mourning of waters. The place occurs in 2 Chronicles 16:4.

strongs.derivation: from H58 (אָבֵל) and H4325 (מַיִם); meadow of water;

entries.name: Abel-meholah
entries.note: H65 gives meadow of dancing, which differs from Hitchcock's mourning of sickness.

strongs.derivation: from H58 (אָבֵל) and H4246 (מְחֹלָה)xlit mᵉchôwlâh corrected to mᵉchôlâh; meadow of dancing;

entries.name: Abel-mizraim
entries.displayMeaning: meadow of Egypt; mourning of Egypt in the narrative
entries.note: H67 gives meadow of Egypt, while Genesis 50:11 expressly associates the name with Egyptian mourning. Preserve the KJV narrative explanation and flag the lexical disagreement instead of replacing Scripture. [Strong H67](https://biblehub.com/hebrew/67.htm).

strongs.derivation: from H58 (אָבֵל) and H4714 (מִצְרַיִם); meadow of Egypt;

entries.name: Abel-shittim
entries.note: H63 gives meadow of the acacias, whereas Hitchcock gives mourning of thorns. Numbers 33:49 names the place.

strongs.derivation: from H58 (אָבֵל) and the plural of H7848 (שִׁטָּה), with the article inserted; meadow of the acacias;
strongs.strongs_def: Abel hash-Shittim, a place in Palestine

entries.name: Abez
entries.note: H77 proposes conspicuous from a probable root meaning gleam; neither egg nor muddy is corroborated.

strongs.derivation: from an unused root probably meaning to gleam; conspicuous;

entries.name: Abi
entries.note: H21 gives fatherly for Hezekiah's mother in 2 Kings 18:2; Hitchcock's my father is a related but different grammatical interpretation. [Strong H21](https://biblehub.com/hebrew/21.htm).

entries.name: Abi-albon
entries.note: H45 explicitly marks its derivation uncertain and probably father of strength; most intelligent father is a competing gloss.

strongs.derivation: from H1 (אָב) and an unused root of uncertain derivation; probably, father of strength (i.e. valiant);

entries.name: Abiah
entries.note: H29 interprets the construction as father/worshipper of Jah; Hitchcock reverses the relation. This records disagreement, not proof of either etymology.

strongs.derivation: or prolonged אֲבִיָּהוּ ; from H1 (אָב) and H3050 (יָהּ); father (i.e. worshipper) of Jah;
strongs.strongs_def: Abijah, the name of several Israelite men and two Israelitesses

entries.name: Abiasaph
entries.note: H23 supports gathering, not the alternative consuming father. [Strong H23](https://biblehub.com/hebrew/23.htm).

strongs.derivation: from H1 (אָב) and H622 (אָסַף); father of gathering (i.e. gatherer);

entries.name: Abiathar
entries.note: H54 gives father of abundance (liberal), rather than excellent father or father of the remnant; G8 refers to that Hebrew name.
hitchcock: excellent father; father of the remnant

strongs.derivation: contracted from H1 (אָב) and H3498 (יָתַר); father of abundance (i.e. liberal);

entries.name: Abib
entries.displayMeaning: Young ear of grain; month Abib
entries.note: H24 supports green ears of grain. In the cited verses this is a month designation; corn here means grain.

strongs.derivation: from an unused root (meaning to be tender);
strongs.strongs_def: green, i.e. a young ear of grain; hence, the name of the month Abib or Nisan
strongs.kjv_def: Abib, ear, green ears of corn (not maize).

entries.name: Abidah
entries.note: H28 explicitly gives father of knowledge; Genesis 25:4 identifies Abraham's descendant through Midian. [Strong H28](https://biblehub.com/hebrew/28.htm).

strongs.derivation: from H1 (אָב) and H3045 (יָדַע); father of knowledge (i.e. knowing);
strongs.strongs_def: Abida, a son of Abraham by Keturah

entries.name: Abidan
entries.note: H27 expressly gives father of judgment; Numbers 1:11 identifies the Benjaminite leader.

strongs.derivation: from H1 (אָב) and H1777 (דִּין); father of judgment (i.e. judge);

entries.name: Abiel
entries.note: H22 interprets father/possessor of God; Hitchcock's God my father reverses the relation. Treat both as lexical proposals.

strongs.derivation: from H1 (אָב) and H410 (אֵל); father (i.e. possessor) of God;
strongs.strongs_def: Abiel, the name of two Israelites

entries.name: Abiezer
entries.note: H44 explicitly gives father of help. Joshua 17:2 and 2 Samuel 23:27 concern different bearers; shared spelling does not identify one person. [Strong H44](https://biblehub.com/hebrew/44.htm).

strongs.derivation: from H1 (אָב) and H5829 (עֵזֶר); father of help (i.e. helpful);
strongs.strongs_def: Abiezer, the name of two Israelites

entries.name: Abigail
entries.note: H26 expressly includes Abigail as an alternate spelling although its KJV field only lists Abigal. Two women share this name; see 1 Samuel 25:3 and 1 Chronicles 2:16.

strongs.derivation: or shorter אֲבִיגַל; from H1 (אָב) and H1524 (גִּיל); father (i.e. source) of joy;
strongs.strongs_def: Abigail or Abigal, the name of two Israelitesses

entries.name: Abihail
entries.note: The compared sources broadly agree on this core sense; this is a lexical proposal, not an assertion about character.

strongs.derivation: or (more correctly) אֲבִיחַיִל ; from H1 (אָב) and H2428 (חַיִל); father (i.e. possessor) of might;
strongs.strongs_def: Abihail or Abichail, the name of three Israelites and two Israelitesses

entries.name: Abihu
entries.note: H30 interprets the components differently from he is my father. [Strong H30](https://biblehub.com/hebrew/30.htm).

strongs.derivation: from H1 (אָב) and H1931 (הוּא); father (i.e. worshipper) of Him (i.e. God);

entries.name: Abihud
entries.note: Strong H31 proposes this sense; Hitchcock: father of praise; confession. These are secondary lexical claims, not the biblical text.

strongs.derivation: from H1 (אָב) and H1935 (הוֹד); father (i.e. possessor) of renown;
strongs.strongs_def: Abihud, the name of two Israelites

entries.name: Abijah
entries.note: The supplied Strong entry differs from Hitchcock or leaves the derivation unresolved; retain source attribution.

strongs.derivation: or prolonged אֲבִיָּהוּ ; from H1 (אָב) and H3050 (יָהּ); father (i.e. worshipper) of Jah;
strongs.strongs_def: Abijah, the name of several Israelite men and two Israelitesses

entries.name: Abijam
entries.note: The pinned Strong H38 record supplies this lexical proposal, compatible with Hitchcock's core sense. This dictionary comparison does not establish the etymology as biblical fact. [Strong H38](https://biblehub.com/hebrew/38.htm).

strongs.derivation: from H1 (אָב) and H3220 (יָם); father of (the) sea (i.e. seaman);
strongs.strongs_def: Abijam (or Abijah), a king of Judah

entries.name: Abilene
entries.note: Strong G9 proposes this sense; Hitchcock: the father of mourning. The derivation remains uncertain.

entries.name: Abimael
entries.note: Strong treats Mael as apparently a tribal name, not sent from God.

strongs.derivation: from H1 (אָב) and an elsewhere unused (probably foreign) word; father of Mael (apparently some Arab tribe);

entries.name: Abimelech
entries.note: H40 lists several bearers; Genesis 20 concerns the Philistine king. [Strong H40](https://biblehub.com/hebrew/40.htm).

strongs.derivation: from H1 (אָב) and H4428 (מֶלֶךְ); father of (the) king;
strongs.strongs_def: Abimelek, the name of two Philistine kings and of two Israelites

entries.name: Abinadab
entries.note: Strong H41 proposes this sense; Hitchcock: father of a vow, or of willingness. These are secondary lexical claims, not the biblical text.
hitchcock: father of a vow, or of willingness

strongs.derivation: from H1 (אָב) and H5068 (נָדַב); father of generosity (i.e. liberal);
strongs.strongs_def: Abinadab, the name of four Israelites

entries.name: Abinoam
entries.note: The compared sources broadly agree on this core sense; this is a lexical proposal, not an assertion about character.

strongs.derivation: from H1 (אָב) and H5278 (נֹעַם); father of pleasantness (i.e. gracious);

entries.name: Abiram
entries.note: Father of deceit is not supported by H48. [Strong H48](https://biblehub.com/hebrew/48.htm).

strongs.derivation: from H1 (אָב) and H7311 (רוּם); father of height (i.e. lofty);
strongs.strongs_def: Abiram, the name of two Israelites

entries.name: Abishag
entries.note: Strong H49 proposes this sense; Hitchcock: ignorance of the father. These are secondary lexical claims, not the biblical text.

strongs.derivation: from H1 (אָב) and H7686 (שָׁגָה); father of error (i.e. blundering);

entries.name: Abishai
entries.note: Hitchcock reverses the father/gift relationship; Strong's generous is explicitly probable.

strongs.derivation: or (shorter) אַבְשַׁי ; from H1 (אָב) and H7862 (שַׁי); father of a gift (i.e. probably generous);

entries.name: Abishalom
entries.note: H53 also covers Absalom; do not merge distinct bearers from shared spelling alone. [Strong H53](https://biblehub.com/hebrew/53.htm).

strongs.derivation: or (shortened) אַבְשָׁלוֹם ; from H1 (אָב) and H7965 (שָׁלוֹם); father of peace (i.e. friendly);
strongs.strongs_def: Abshalom, a son of David; also (the fuller form) a later Israelite

entries.name: Abishua
entries.note: Strong H50 proposes this sense; Hitchcock: father of salvation. These are secondary lexical claims, not the biblical text.

strongs.derivation: from H1 (אָב) and H7771 (שׁוֹעַ); father of plenty (i.e. prosperous);
strongs.strongs_def: Abishua, the name of two Israelites

entries.name: Abishur
entries.note: The wall sense agrees; uprightness is not supported by H51.
hitchcock: father of the wall; father of uprightness

strongs.derivation: from H1 (אָב) and H7791 (שׁוּר); father of (the) wall (i.e. perhaps mason);

entries.name: Abital
entries.note: H37 supports dew, not the shadow alternative. [Strong H37](https://biblehub.com/hebrew/37.htm).
hitchcock: the father of the dew; or of the shadow

strongs.derivation: from H1 (אָב) and H2919 (טַל); father of dew (i.e. fresh);
strongs.strongs_def: Abital, a wife of King David

entries.name: Abitub
entries.note: Strong H36 proposes this sense; Hitchcock: father of goodness. These are secondary lexical claims, not the biblical text.

strongs.derivation: from H1 (אָב) and H2898 (טוּב); father of goodness (i.e. good);

entries.name: Abiud
entries.note: G10 refers to H31; praise is a loose rendering of renown, not a separate proven derivation.

strongs.derivation: from H1 (אָב) and H1935 (הוֹד); father (i.e. possessor) of renown;
strongs.strongs_def: Abihud, the name of two Israelites

entries.name: Abner
entries.note: The pinned Strong H74 record supplies this lexical proposal, compatible with Hitchcock's core sense. This dictionary comparison does not establish the etymology as biblical fact. [Strong H74](https://biblehub.com/hebrew/74.htm).

strongs.derivation: or (fully) אֲבִינֵר ; from H1 (אָב) and H5216 (נִיר); father of light (i.e. enlightening);

entries.name: Abraham
entries.note: Strong H85, G11 proposes this sense; Hitchcock: father of a great multitude. These are secondary lexical claims, not the biblical text.

strongs.derivation: contracted from H1 (אָב) and an unused root (probably meaning to be populous); father of a multitude;
strongs.strongs_def: Abraham, the later name of Abram

entries.name: Abram
entries.note: The compared sources broadly agree on this core sense; this is a lexical proposal, not an assertion about character.

strongs.strongs_def: Abram, the original name of Abraham

entries.name: Absalom
entries.note: The pinned Strong H53 record supplies this lexical proposal, compatible with Hitchcock's core sense. This dictionary comparison does not establish the etymology as biblical fact. [Strong H53](https://biblehub.com/hebrew/53.htm).

strongs.derivation: or (shortened) אַבְשָׁלוֹם ; from H1 (אָב) and H7965 (שָׁלוֹם); father of peace (i.e. friendly);
strongs.strongs_def: Abshalom, a son of David; also (the fuller form) a later Israelite

entries.name: Accad
entries.note: Strong H390 proposes this sense; Hitchcock: a vessel; pitcher; spark. These are secondary lexical claims, not the biblical text.

strongs.derivation: from an unused root probably meaning to strengthen; a fortress;

entries.name: Accho
entries.note: H5910 describes only an apparent derivation from an unused root.

strongs.derivation: apparently from an unused root meaning to hem in;
strongs.strongs_def: Akko (from its situation on a bay)

entries.name: Aceldama
entries.note: Acts 1:19 also expressly interprets the place-name. [Strong G184](https://biblehub.com/greek/184.htm).

strongs.strongs_def: corresponding to H02506 and H01818); Akeldama, a place near Jerusalem
strongs.derivation: of Chaldee origin (meaning field of blood;

entries.name: Achab
entries.note: The pinned snapshot H256 prints Achab in its description, corresponding to KJV Ahab (Jeremiah 29:22). Brother of his father is its lexical proposal; exact Achab is not established as a separate KJV spelling or person.

strongs.derivation: once (by contraction) אֶחָב (Jeremiah 29:22); from H251 (אָח) and H1 (אָב); brother (i.e. friend) of (his) father;
strongs.strongs_def: Achab, the name of a king of Israel and of a prophet at Babylon

entries.name: Achaia
entries.note: The supplied Strong entry differs from Hitchcock or leaves the derivation unresolved; retain source attribution.

strongs.strongs_def: Achaia (i.e. Greece), a country of Europe

entries.name: Achaicus
entries.note: G883 supports the geographical description, not sorrowing or sad. [Strong G883](https://biblehub.com/greek/883.htm).
hitchcock: a native of Achaia; sorrowing; sad

entries.name: Achan
entries.note: Strong H5912 (Achan) and H5917 (Achar) are variants; Joshua 7:1 and 1 Chronicles 2:7 ground the identification.

strongs.derivation: from an unused root meaning to trouble; troublesome;

entries.name: Achaz
entries.note: G881 points to H271, which gives possessor.

strongs.strongs_def: Achaz, the name of a Jewish king and of an Israelite

entries.name: Achbor
entries.note: H5907 refers to H5909 mouse; bruising is unsupported. [Strong H5907](https://biblehub.com/hebrew/5907.htm).

strongs.strongs_def: Akbor, the name of an Idumaean and of two Israelites

entries.name: Achim
entries.note: Strong G885 proposes this sense; Hitchcock: preparing; revenging; confirming. The derivation remains uncertain.

entries.name: Achish
entries.note: The supplied Strong entry differs from Hitchcock or leaves the derivation unresolved; retain source attribution.
hitchcock: thus it is; how is this

entries.name: Achmetha
entries.note: H307 calls the name Persian; brother of death is not established. [Strong H307](https://biblehub.com/hebrew/307.htm).

strongs.strongs_def: Achmetha (i.e. Ecbatana), the summer capital of Persia

entries.name: Achor
entries.note: Strong H5911 proposes this sense; Hitchcock: trouble. These are secondary lexical claims, not the biblical text.

strongs.strongs_def: Akor, the name of a place in Palestine

entries.name: Achsah
entries.note: H5915 names an ornament, not bursting a veil; adorned is only a related idea.

entries.name: Achshaph
entries.note: H407 derives it from witchcraft, not poison; tricks is at best an imprecise association. [Strong H407](https://biblehub.com/hebrew/407.htm).

entries.name: Achzib
entries.note: Strong explains a failing winter torrent; Hitchcock's one that runs is not established. Two places share the spelling.

strongs.derivation: from H391 (אַכְזָב); deceitful (in the sense of a winter-torrent which fails in summer);
strongs.strongs_def: Akzib, the name of two places in Palestine

entries.name: Adadah
entries.note: The supplied Strong entry differs from Hitchcock or leaves the derivation unresolved; retain source attribution.

entries.name: Adah
entries.note: H5711 conflicts with an assembly. [Strong H5711](https://biblehub.com/hebrew/5711.htm).

strongs.strongs_def: Adah, the name of two women

entries.name: Adaiah
entries.note: Strong H5718 proposes this sense; Hitchcock: the witness of the Lord. These are secondary lexical claims, not the biblical text.

strongs.derivation: or עֲדָיָהוּ; from H5710 (עָדָה) and H3050 (יָהּ); Jah has adorned;
strongs.strongs_def: Adajah, the name of eight Israelites

entries.name: Adaliah
entries.note: H118 identifies Adalia as Haman's son and gives Persian origin; the multiple Hebrew-looking Hitchcock meanings are uncorroborated.
hitchcock: one that draws water; poverty; cloud; death

entries.name: Adam
entries.note: H121 refers to H120 ruddy/human; earthy is a related traditional interpretation. Joshua 3:16 names a town, distinct from the first man. [Strong H121](https://biblehub.com/hebrew/121.htm); [Strong G76](https://biblehub.com/greek/76.htm).

strongs.strongs_def: Adam the name of the first man, also of a place in Palestine
Adam, the first man; typically (of Jesus) man (as his representative)

entries.name: Adamah
entries.note: H128 refers to H127, soil from its redness; of blood is not supplied by these entries.

entries.name: Adami
entries.note: H129 supports earthy; other Hitchcock alternatives are not each established.

entries.name: Adar
entries.displayMeaning: month Adar: perhaps fire; place Adar: ample
entries.note: H143/H144 denote the month. Joshua 15:3 denotes the place Adar (related to Addar H146); do not apply the month entry to that location. [Strong H143](https://biblehub.com/hebrew/143.htm); [Strong H144](https://biblehub.com/hebrew/144.htm); [Strong H146](https://biblehub.com/hebrew/146.htm).

strongs.derivation: probably of foreign derivation; perhaps meaning fire;

strongs.strongs_def: Addar, a place in Palestine; also an Israelite

entries.name: Adbeel
entries.note: Strong H110 proposes this sense; Hitchcock: vapor, or cloud of God. These are secondary lexical claims, not the biblical text.

strongs.derivation: probably from H109 (אָדַב) (in the sense of chastisement) and H410 (אֵל); disciplined of God;

entries.name: Addi
entries.note: G78 only probably derives the name from Hebrew, comparing ornament H5716.

strongs.derivation: from H5710 (עָדָה) in the sense of trappings;
strongs.strongs_def: finery; generally an outfit; specifically, a headstall

entries.name: Addin
entries.note: No supplied KJV reference or exact Strong entry establishes Addin; possible spelling relation to Adin remains unconfirmed.

entries.name: Addon
entries.note: Strong H114 proposes this sense; Hitchcock: basis; foundation; the Lord. These are secondary lexical claims, not the biblical text.

entries.name: Adiel
entries.note: Witness is a different root from the one H5717 proposes.

strongs.derivation: from H5716 (עֲדִי) and H410 (אֵל); ornament of God;
strongs.strongs_def: Adiel, the name of three Israelites

entries.name: Adin
entries.note: H5720 points to H5719; adorned is not supported by that derivation. [Strong H5720](https://biblehub.com/hebrew/5720.htm).

strongs.strongs_def: Adin, the name of two Israelites

entries.name: Adithaim
entries.note: Strong H5723 proposes this sense; Hitchcock: assemblies; testimonies. These are secondary lexical claims, not the biblical text.

strongs.derivation: dual of a feminine of H5706 (עַד); double prey;

entries.name: Adlai
entries.note: The supplied Strong entry differs from Hitchcock or leaves the derivation unresolved; retain source attribution.

strongs.derivation: probably from an unused root of uncertain meaning;

entries.name: Admah
entries.note: H126 supports earthy; bloody is not its stated name gloss. [Strong H126](https://biblehub.com/hebrew/126.htm).

strongs.strongs_def: Admah, a place near the Dead Sea

entries.name: Admatha
entries.note: Strong H133 proposes this sense; Hitchcock: a cloud of death; a mortal vapor. The derivation remains uncertain.
hitchcock: a cloud of death; a mortal vapor

entries.name: Adna
entries.note: The compared sources broadly agree on this core sense; this is a lexical proposal, not an assertion about character.

strongs.strongs_def: Adna, the name of two Israelites

entries.name: Adnah
entries.note: H5734 does not give eternal rest. [Strong H5734](https://biblehub.com/hebrew/5734.htm).

strongs.strongs_def: Adnah, the name of two Israelites

entries.name: Adoni-bezek
entries.note: Strong refers to a ruler of the place Bezek, not a declaration that the name means the LORD's lightning.
hitchcock: the lightning of the Lord; the Lord of lightning

strongs.derivation: from H113 (אָדוֹן) and H966 (בֶּזֶק); lord of Bezek;

entries.name: Adoni-zedek
entries.note: Hyphenated input corresponds to KJV Adonizedec, H139; justice of the Lord reverses the relation.
hitchcock: justice of the Lord; lord of justice

strongs.derivation: from H113 (אָדוֹן) and H6664 (צֶדֶק); lord of justice;

entries.name: Adonijah
entries.note: H138's component interpretation differs from the Lord is my master; preserve both as attributed proposals. [Strong H138](https://biblehub.com/hebrew/138.htm).

strongs.derivation: original (prolonged) אֲדֹנִיָּהוּ ; from H113 (אָדוֹן) and H3050 (יָהּ); lord (i.e. worshipper) of Jah;
strongs.strongs_def: Adonijah, the name of three Israelites

entries.name: Adonikam
entries.note: Strong H140 proposes this sense; Hitchcock: the Lord is raised. These are secondary lexical claims, not the biblical text.

strongs.derivation: from H113 (אָדוֹן) and H6965 (קוּם); lord of rising (i.e. high);
strongs.strongs_def: Adonikam, the name of one or two Israelites

entries.name: Adoniram
entries.note: The compared sources broadly agree on this core sense; this is a lexical proposal, not an assertion about character.
hitchcock: my Lord is most high; Lord of might and elevation

strongs.derivation: from H113 (אָדוֹן) and H7311 (רוּם); lord of height;

entries.name: Adoraim
entries.note: H115 conflicts with strength of the sea. [Strong H115](https://biblehub.com/hebrew/115.htm).

strongs.derivation: dual from H142 (אָדַר) (in the sense of eminence); double mound;

entries.name: Adoram
entries.note: H151 is a contraction of Adoniram H141, not their beauty or power.

strongs.derivation: from H113 (אָדוֹן) and H7311 (רוּם); lord of height;

entries.name: Adrammelech
entries.note: H152 covers both a deity (2 Kings 17:31) and Sennacherib's son (2 Kings 19:37); keep identities separate.
hitchcock: the cloak, glory, grandeur or power of the king

strongs.derivation: from H142 (אָדַר) and H4428 (מֶלֶךְ); splendor of (the) king;
strongs.strongs_def: Adrammelek, the name of an Assyrian idol, also of a son of Sennacherib

entries.name: Adramyttium
entries.note: G98 is an adjective for the ship's origin in Acts 27:2; it supplies no court of death etymology. [Strong G98](https://biblehub.com/greek/98.htm).

entries.name: Adriel
entries.note: Strong H5741 proposes this sense; Hitchcock: the flock of God. These are secondary lexical claims, not the biblical text.

strongs.derivation: from H5739 (עֵדֶר) and H410 (אֵל); flock of God;

entries.name: Adullam
entries.note: H5725 proposes a relation to H5724, whose root meaning is uncertain; three confident meanings are unwarranted.
hitchcock: their testimony; their prey; their ornament

strongs.derivation: probably from the passive participle of the same as H5724 (עַדְלַי);

entries.name: Adummim
entries.note: H131 supports the red sense, with the place identified as a pass. [Strong H131](https://biblehub.com/hebrew/131.htm).

entries.name: Aeneas
entries.note: The transcription prints AEneas (ligature form); G132 expressly says uncertain derivation. Acts 9:33 identifies the man.

entries.name: Aenon
entries.note: G137 gives Aenon (digital spelling AEnon) as place of springs, but its G5869 root prefix is corrupt: Hebrew H5869 is intended. Cloud is uncorroborated.

strongs.derivation: of Hebrew origin (a derivative of G5869, place of springs);

strongs.strongs_def: an eye (literally or figuratively); by analogy, a fountain (as the eye of the landscape)
strongs.kjv_def: affliction, outward appearance, [phrase] before, [phrase] think best, colour, conceit, [phrase] be content, countenance, [phrase] displease, eye((-brow), (-d), -sight), face, [phrase] favour, fountain, furrow (from the margin), [idiom] him, [phrase] humble, knowledge, look, ([phrase] well), [idiom] me, open(-ly), [phrase] (not) please, presence, [phrase] regard, resemblance, sight, [idiom] thee, [idiom] them, [phrase] think, [idiom] us, well, [idiom] you(-rselves).

entries.name: Agabus
entries.note: G13 only compares Hebrew H2285 (Hagab, locust). Father's joy/feast is not established. [Strong G13](https://biblehub.com/greek/13.htm).
hitchcock: a locust; the father's joy or feast

entries.name: Agag
entries.note: Strong marks the derivation uncertain and describes a royal title; roof is a competing gloss, not settled by these sources.

strongs.derivation: or אֲגָג; of uncertain derivation (compare H89 (אָגֵא)); flame;
strongs.strongs_def: Agag, a title of Amalekitish kings

entries.name: Agar
entries.note: KJV Galatians' Agar corresponds to Greek G28 Hagar, referring to Hebrew H1904; H1904 expressly leaves the derivation uncertain.
hitchcock: or Hagar, a stranger; one that fears

entries.name: Agee
entries.note: H89 explicitly marks derivation uncertain. [Strong H89](https://biblehub.com/hebrew/89.htm).

entries.name: Agrippa
entries.note: Strong's apparent derivation competes with Hitchcock's birth-pain explanation; neither is a biblical assertion.
hitchcock: one who causes great pain at his birth

strongs.strongs_def: wild-horse tamer; Agrippas, one of the Herods

entries.name: Agur
entries.note: The gathered sense agrees. Strong's identification as a fanciful name for Solomon is historical commentary, not stated by Proverbs 30:1.

strongs.derivation: passive participle of H103 (אָגַר); gathered (i.e. received among the sages);
strongs.strongs_def: Agur, a fanciful name for Solomon

entries.name: Ahab
entries.displayMeaning: brother or friend of his father
entries.note: H256's brother of father is broadly compatible with uncle; there are distinct Ahab bearers. [Strong H256](https://biblehub.com/hebrew/256.htm).

strongs.derivation: once (by contraction) אֶחָב (Jeremiah 29:22); from H251 (אָח) and H1 (אָב); brother (i.e. friend) of (his) father;
strongs.strongs_def: Achab, the name of a king of Israel and of a prophet at Babylon

entries.name: Aharah
entries.note: Strong H315 proposes this sense; Hitchcock: a smiling brother; a meadow of a sweet savor. These are secondary lexical claims, not the biblical text.
hitchcock: a smiling brother; a meadow of a sweet savor

strongs.derivation: from H310 (אַחַר) and H251 (אָח); after (his) brother;

entries.name: Aharhel
entries.note: The supplied Strong entry differs from Hitchcock or leaves the derivation unresolved; retain source attribution.
hitchcock: another host; the last sorrow; a brother's sheep

strongs.derivation: from H310 (אַחַר) and H2426 (חֵיל); behind (the) intrenchment (i.e. safe);

entries.name: Ahasbai
entries.note: H308 explicitly marks derivation uncertain. [Strong H308](https://biblehub.com/hebrew/308.htm).
hitchcock: trusting in me; a grown-up brother

entries.name: Ahasuerus
entries.note: Strong describes a title rather than name. Ezra 4:6 and Esther 1:1 require historical identity care; do not merge rulers solely by spelling.

strongs.strongs_def: Achashverosh (i.e. Ahasuerus or Artaxerxes, but in this case Xerxes), the title (rather than name) of a Persian king

entries.name: Ahava
entries.note: The supplied Strong entry differs from Hitchcock or leaves the derivation unresolved; retain source attribution.

entries.name: Ahaz
entries.note: The pinned Strong H271 record supplies this lexical proposal, compatible with Hitchcock's core sense. This dictionary comparison does not establish the etymology as biblical fact. [Strong H271](https://biblehub.com/hebrew/271.htm).

strongs.strongs_def: Achaz, the name of a Jewish king and of an Israelite

entries.name: Ahaziah
entries.note: Strong supports seized, not the alternate vision; kings of Israel and Judah share the name.

strongs.derivation: or (prolonged) אֲחַזְיָהוּ ; from H270 (אָחַז) and H3050 (יָהּ); Jah has seized;
strongs.strongs_def: Achazjah, the name of a Jewish and an Israelite king

entries.name: Ahi
entries.note: The compared sources broadly agree on this core sense; this is a lexical proposal, not an assertion about character.

strongs.strongs_def: Achi, the name of two Israelites

entries.name: Ahiah
entries.note: The pinned Strong H281 record supplies this lexical proposal, compatible with Hitchcock's core sense. This dictionary comparison does not establish the etymology as biblical fact. [Strong H281](https://biblehub.com/hebrew/281.htm).

strongs.derivation: or (prolonged) אֲחִיָּהוּ ; from H251 (אָח) and H3050 (יָהּ); brother (i.e. worshipper) of Jah;
strongs.strongs_def: Achijah, the name of nine Israelites

entries.name: Ahiam
entries.note: Strong H279 proposes this sense; Hitchcock: mother's brother; brother of a nation. These are secondary lexical claims, not the biblical text.
hitchcock: mother's brother; brother of a nation

strongs.derivation: from H251 (אָח) and H517 (אֵם); brother of the mother (i.e. uncle);

entries.name: Ahian
entries.note: H291 supplies no wine element.

entries.name: Ahiezer
entries.note: The pinned Strong H295 record supplies this lexical proposal, compatible with Hitchcock's core sense. This dictionary comparison does not establish the etymology as biblical fact. [Strong H295](https://biblehub.com/hebrew/295.htm).

strongs.derivation: from H251 (אָח) and H5828 (עֵזֶר); brother of help;
strongs.strongs_def: Achiezer, the name of two Israelites

entries.name: Ahihud
entries.note: Numbers 34:27 uses H282 (brother of renown); 1 Chronicles 8:7 uses H284 (brother of a riddle). One English spelling conceals distinct Hebrew forms.
hitchcock: brother of vanity, or of darkness, or of joy, or of praise; witty brother

strongs.derivation: from H251 (אָח) and H1935 (הוֹד); brother (i.e. possessor) of renown;
from H251 (אָח) and H2330 (חוּד); brother of a riddle (i.e. mysterious);

entries.name: Ahijah
entries.note: Hitchcock is only a cross-reference to Ahiah, not an independent meaning; H281 proposes brother/worshipper of Jah.

strongs.derivation: or (prolonged) אֲחִיָּהוּ ; from H251 (אָח) and H3050 (יָהּ); brother (i.e. worshipper) of Jah;
strongs.strongs_def: Achijah, the name of nine Israelites

entries.name: Ahikam
entries.note: H296 supports rising, not the avenges alternative. [Strong H296](https://biblehub.com/hebrew/296.htm).
hitchcock: a brother who raises up or avenges

strongs.derivation: from H251 (אָח) and H6965 (קוּם); brother of rising (i.e. high);

entries.name: Ahilud
entries.note: Strong H286 proposes this sense; Hitchcock: a brother born, or begotten. These are secondary lexical claims, not the biblical text.

strongs.derivation: from H251 (אָח) and H3205 (יָלַד); brother of one born;

entries.name: Ahimaaz
entries.note: The supplied Strong entry differs from Hitchcock or leaves the derivation unresolved; retain source attribution.

strongs.derivation: from H251 (אָח) and the equivalent of H4619 (מַעַץ); brother of anger;
strongs.strongs_def: Achimaats, the name of three Israelites

entries.name: Ahiman
entries.note: H289 conflicts with brother of the right hand. [Strong H289](https://biblehub.com/hebrew/289.htm).

strongs.derivation: or אֲחִימָן ; from H251 (אָח) and H4480 (מִן); brother of a portion (i.e. gift);
strongs.strongs_def: Achiman, the name of an Anakite and of an Israelite

entries.name: Ahimelech
entries.note: Strong H288 proposes this sense; Hitchcock: my brother is a king; my king's brother. These are secondary lexical claims, not the biblical text.
hitchcock: my brother is a king; my king's brother

strongs.derivation: from H251 (אָח) and H4428 (מֶלֶךְ); brother of (the) king;
strongs.strongs_def: Achimelek, the name of an Israelite and of a Hittite

entries.name: Ahimoth
entries.note: The compared sources broadly agree on this core sense; this is a lexical proposal, not an assertion about character.

strongs.derivation: from H251 (אָח) and H4191 (מוּת); brother of death;

entries.name: Ahinadab
entries.note: H292 supports willingness/liberality, not brother of a vow. [Strong H292](https://biblehub.com/hebrew/292.htm).
hitchcock: a willing brother; brother of a vow

strongs.derivation: from H251 (אָח) and H5068 (נָדַב); brother of liberality;

entries.name: Ahinoam
entries.note: Strong H293 proposes this sense; Hitchcock: beauty of the brother; brother of motion. These are secondary lexical claims, not the biblical text.
hitchcock: beauty of the brother; brother of motion

strongs.derivation: from H251 (אָח) and H5278 (נֹעַם); brother of pleasantness;
strongs.strongs_def: Achinoam, the name of two Israelitesses

entries.name: Ahio
entries.note: The compared sources broadly agree on this core sense; this is a lexical proposal, not an assertion about character.

strongs.strongs_def: Achio, the name of three Israelites

entries.name: Ahira
entries.note: H299 supports iniquity, not shepherd. A lexical proposal is not a moral judgment about the bearer. [Strong H299](https://biblehub.com/hebrew/299.htm).
hitchcock: brother of iniquity; brother of the shepherd

strongs.derivation: from H251 (אָח) and H7451 (רַע); brother of wrong;

entries.name: Ahiram
entries.note: Strong H297 proposes this sense; Hitchcock: brother of craft, or of protection. These are secondary lexical claims, not the biblical text.
hitchcock: brother of craft, or of protection

strongs.derivation: from H251 (אָח) and H7311 (רוּם); brother of height (i.e. high);

entries.name: Ahisamach
entries.note: The compared sources broadly agree on this core sense; this is a lexical proposal, not an assertion about character.

strongs.derivation: from H251 (אָח) and H5564 (סָמַךְ); brother of support;

entries.name: Ahishahur
entries.note: Ahishahur has no supplied KJV reference or exact Strong identification; do not silently normalize to Ahishahar.
hitchcock: brother of the morning or dew; brother of blackness

entries.name: Ahishar
entries.note: H301 belongs to Ahishar (1 Kings 4:6); supplied H300 is Ahishahar, a different name, and must not determine this gloss. Prince is unsupported.
hitchcock: brother of a prince; brother of a song

strongs.derivation: from H251 (אָח) and H7891 (שִׁיר); brother of (the) singer;

entries.name: Ahithophel
entries.note: Folly agrees; ruin is not separately supplied by H302.

strongs.derivation: from H251 (אָח) and H8602 (תָּפֵל); brother of folly;

entries.name: Ahitub
entries.note: The pinned Strong H285 record supplies this lexical proposal, compatible with Hitchcock's core sense. This dictionary comparison does not establish the etymology as biblical fact. [Strong H285](https://biblehub.com/hebrew/285.htm).

strongs.derivation: from H251 (אָח) and H2898 (טוּב); brother of goodness;
strongs.strongs_def: Achitub, the name of several priests

entries.name: Ahlab
entries.note: Strong H303 proposes this sense; Hitchcock: made of milk, or of fat; brother of the heart. These are secondary lexical claims, not the biblical text.
hitchcock: made of milk, or of fat; brother of the heart

strongs.derivation: from the same root as H2459 (חֶלֶב); fatness (i.e. fertile);

entries.name: Ahlai
entries.note: Expecting/beseeching loosely agrees with wishful; sorrow is not independently supported.

strongs.strongs_def: Achlai, the name of an Israelitess and of an Israelite

entries.name: Ahoah
entries.note: H265 does not support live brother or thorn/thistle. [Strong H265](https://biblehub.com/hebrew/265.htm).
hitchcock: a live brother; my thorn or thistle

entries.name: Aholah
entries.note: Strong's feminine possessive is her tent; Ezekiel 23:4 expressly applies Aholah to Samaria. His tent is a different pronoun.

strongs.derivation: in form a feminine of H168 (אֹהֶל), but in fact for אׇהֳלָהּ; from H168 (אֹהֶל); her tent (i.e. idolatrous sanctuary);
strongs.strongs_def: Oholah, a symbolic name for Samaria

entries.name: Aholiab
entries.note: The compared sources broadly agree on this core sense; this is a lexical proposal, not an assertion about character.

strongs.derivation: from H168 (אֹהֶל) and H1 (אָב); tent of (his) father;

entries.name: Aholibah
entries.note: Ezekiel 23:4 identifies this as a symbolic name for Jerusalem; Strong's summary says Judah. [Strong H172](https://biblehub.com/hebrew/172.htm).
hitchcock: my tent, or my tabernacle, in her

strongs.derivation: (similarly with H170 (אׇהֳלָה)) for אׇהֳלִיבָהּ ; from H168 (אֹהֶל); my tent (is) in her;
strongs.strongs_def: Oholibah, a symbolic name for Judah

entries.name: Aholibamah
entries.note: Strong H173 proposes this sense; Hitchcock: my tabernacle is exalted. These are secondary lexical claims, not the biblical text.

strongs.derivation: from H168 (אֹהֶל) and H1116 (בָּמָה); tent of (the) height;

entries.name: Ahumai
entries.note: H267 expressly qualifies its derivation with perhaps.
hitchcock: a meadow of waters; a brother of waters

strongs.derivation: perhaps from H251 (אָח) and H4325 (מַיִם); brother (i.e. neighbour) of water;

entries.name: Ahuzam
entries.note: H275 supports taking, but not the added vision. [Strong H275](https://biblehub.com/hebrew/275.htm).

entries.name: Ahuzzah
entries.note: H276 identifies Ahuzzath (Genesis 26:26), not the exact Ahuzzah spelling. It proposes possession; seizing/collecting are not separately established. This is a spelling proposal, not an exact match.

entries.name: Ai
entries.note: H5857 is the place-name candidate; H5892 is the ordinary word city and should not supply a second name etymology.

strongs.derivation: or (feminine) עַיָּא; (Nehemiah 11:31), or עַיָּת; (Isaiah 10:28), for H5856 (עִי);
strongs.strongs_def: Ai, Aja or Ajath, a place in Palestine

strongs.derivation: or (in the plural) עָר; or עָיַר; (Judges 10:4), from H5782 (עוּר)
strongs.strongs_def: a city (a place guarded by waking or a watch) in the widest sense (even of a mere encampment or post)
strongs.kjv_def: Ai (from margin), city, court (from margin), town.

entries.name: Aiah
entries.note: H345 points to H344; raven, isle and alas are not established for this name. [Strong H345](https://biblehub.com/hebrew/345.htm).
hitchcock: vulture, raven; an isle; alas, where is it?

strongs.strongs_def: Ajah, the name of two Israelites

entries.name: Aiath
entries.note: H5857 explicitly cites Isaiah 10:28's variant and points to H5856, ruin; hour, eye and fountain are not established here.
hitchcock: same as Ai; an hour; eye; fountain

strongs.derivation: or (feminine) עַיָּא; (Nehemiah 11:31), or עַיָּת; (Isaiah 10:28), for H5856 (עִי);
strongs.strongs_def: Ai, Aja or Ajath, a place in Palestine

entries.name: Aijeleth-Shahar
entries.note: H365/H355 give doe and H7837 dawn; Hitchcock's land is not supported. This is the Psalm 22 musical heading, not a person. The local KJV data appends that heading to Psalm 21:13; do not cite that verse as its canonical location.

strongs.kjv_def: day(-spring), early, light, morning, whence riseth.

entries.name: Ain
entries.note: H5871 does not identify Ain with Aiath; this is a significant cross-reference error. [Strong H5871](https://biblehub.com/hebrew/5871.htm).

strongs.strongs_def: Ajin, the name (thus simply) of two places in Palestine

entries.name: Ajalon
entries.note: Strong supports the deer element; chain and strength are not established. The source recognizes several places.

strongs.strongs_def: Ajalon, the name of five places in Palestine

entries.name: Akkub
entries.note: H6126 does not substantiate the entire list, especially lewdness.

strongs.strongs_def: Akkub, the name of five Israelites

entries.name: Akrabbim
entries.note: H4610 is the compound Maaleh-acrabbim; Akrabbim is its scorpions component, not a personal name. [Strong H4610](https://biblehub.com/hebrew/4610.htm).

strongs.derivation: from H4608 (מַעֲלֶה) and (the plural of) H6137 (עַקְרָב);
strongs.strongs_def: Steep of Scorpions, a place in the Desert
strongs.kjv_def: Maaleh-accrabim, the ascent (going up) of Akrabbim.

entries.name: Alammelech
entries.note: Strong H487 proposes this sense; Hitchcock: God is king. These are secondary lexical claims, not the biblical text.

strongs.derivation: from H427 (אַלָּה) and H4428 (מֶלֶךְ); oak of (the) king;

entries.name: Alemeth
entries.note: H5964 covers both a place and people; do not conflate their identities or append worlds/dead as established senses.
hitchcock: hiding; youth; worlds; upon the dead

strongs.strongs_def: Alemeth, the name of a place in Palestine and of two Israelites

entries.name: Alexander
entries.note: G223 supports assisting/defending men; the supplied references concern several bearers. [Strong G223](https://biblehub.com/greek/223.htm).

strongs.strongs_def: man-defender; Alexander, the name of three Israelites and one other man
strongs.derivation: from the same as (the first part of) G220 (ἀλέκτωρ) and G435 (ἀνήρ);

entries.name: Alian
entries.note: Strong H5935 proposes this sense; Hitchcock: high. These are secondary lexical claims, not the biblical text.

entries.name: Alleluia
entries.note: A liturgical exclamation in Revelation 19, not a person's name; no exact candidate was supplied.

entries.name: Allon
entries.note: H438 points to H437 oak; strong is an associative expansion. [Strong H438](https://biblehub.com/hebrew/438.htm).

strongs.strongs_def: Allon, an Israelite, also a place in Palestine

entries.name: Allon-bachuth
entries.note: Strong H439 proposes this sense; Hitchcock: the oak of weeping. These are secondary lexical claims, not the biblical text.

strongs.derivation: from H437 (אַלּוֹן) and a variation of H1068 (בְּכִית); oak of weeping;

entries.name: Almodad
entries.note: The supplied Strong entry differs from Hitchcock or leaves the derivation unresolved; retain source attribution.

entries.name: Almon
entries.note: H5960 lacks a kjv_def field in the digital file but explicitly identifies Almon and gives hidden. [Strong H5960](https://biblehub.com/hebrew/5960.htm).

strongs.derivation: from H5956 (עָלַם); hidden; See also H5963 (עַלְמֹן דִּבְלָתָיְמָה).

entries.name: Almon-diblathaim
entries.note: H5963 gives a compound place designation, with its KJV field misspelt Almondilathaim. Hidden in a cluster of fig trees is not established by that entry; Numbers 33:46 names the station.
hitchcock: hidden in a cluster of fig trees

strongs.derivation: from the same as H5960 (עַלְמוֹן) and the dual of H1960 (הֻיְּדָה) (compare H1015 (בֵּית דִּבְלָתַיִם)) with enclitic of direction; Almon towards Diblathajim;

entries.name: Alpheus
entries.note: G256 compares H2501, whose derivation is change; the input spelling has no supplied KJV reference.

entries.name: Alush
entries.note: H442 explicitly marks derivation uncertain. [Strong H442](https://biblehub.com/hebrew/442.htm).

strongs.strongs_def: Alush, a place in the Desert

entries.name: Alvah
entries.note: Strong relates H5933 to H5932 (moral perverseness), disagreeing with Hitchcock's highness. Retain the attributed alternatives; this is an etymological proposal, not a judgment about the person.

strongs.derivation: or עַליָה; the same as H5932 (עַלְוָה);

entries.name: Amad
entries.note: The supplied Strong entry differs from Hitchcock or leaves the derivation unresolved; retain source attribution.

strongs.derivation: from H5971 (עַם) and H5703 (עַד); people of time;

entries.name: Amal
entries.note: H6000 points to H5999, whose KJV renderings include labour and iniquity. This does not establish the bearer's character. [Strong H6000](https://biblehub.com/hebrew/6000.htm).

entries.name: Amalek
entries.note: Strong H6002 proposes this sense; Hitchcock: a people that licks up. The derivation remains uncertain.

strongs.strongs_def: Amalek, a descendant of Esau; also his posterity and their country

entries.name: Aman
entries.note: No exact candidate or KJV occurrence supplied.

entries.name: Amana
entries.note: H549 points to H548 something fixed/covenant; nurse is unsupported. [Strong H549](https://biblehub.com/hebrew/549.htm).

entries.name: Amariah
entries.note: Strong supports the Lord says portion; integrity is not established by this derivation.
hitchcock: the Lord says; the integrity of the Lord

strongs.derivation: or prolonged אֲמַרְיָהוּ; from H559 (אָמַר) and H3050 (יָהּ); Jah has said (i.e. promised);
strongs.strongs_def: Amarjah, the name of nine Israelites

entries.name: Amasa
entries.note: The supplied Strong entry differs from Hitchcock or leaves the derivation unresolved; retain source attribution.

strongs.strongs_def: Amasa, the name of two Israelites

entries.name: Amasai
entries.note: H6022 conflicts with strong. [Strong H6022](https://biblehub.com/hebrew/6022.htm).

strongs.strongs_def: Amasai, the name of three Israelites

entries.name: Amashai
entries.note: Strong H6023 proposes this sense; Hitchcock: the people's gift. These are secondary lexical claims, not the biblical text.

entries.name: Amashi-ali
entries.note: The printed cross-reference form is unlocated in the supplied KJV references; do not treat as an independently established biblical name.

entries.name: Amaziah
entries.note: The pinned Strong H558 record supplies this lexical proposal, compatible with Hitchcock's core sense. This dictionary comparison does not establish the etymology as biblical fact. [Strong H558](https://biblehub.com/hebrew/558.htm).

strongs.derivation: or אֲמַצְיָהוּ; from H553 (אָמַץ) and H3050 (יָהּ); strength of Jah;
strongs.strongs_def: Amatsjah, the name of four Israelites

entries.name: Ami
entries.note: Strong treats Ami as an abbreviated Amon, not a compound of mother, fear or people.

strongs.strongs_def: Amon, the name of three Israelites

entries.name: Aminadab
entries.note: G284 points to H5992; Hitchcock supplies a cross-reference rather than a meaning.

strongs.derivation: from H5971 (עַם) and H5068 (נָדַב); people of liberality;
strongs.strongs_def: Amminadab, the name of four Israelites

entries.name: Amittai
entries.note: H573 supports true, not fearing. [Strong H573](https://biblehub.com/hebrew/573.htm).

entries.name: Ammah
entries.note: Strong relates the hill's name to H520, a cubit; Hitchcock's possessive people gloss is unsupported by that relationship.

strongs.strongs_def: properly, a mother (i.e. unit of measure, or the fore-arm (below the elbow), i.e. a cubit; also a door-base (as a bond of the entrance)
strongs.kjv_def: cubit, [phrase] hundred (by exchange for H3967 (מֵאָה)), measure, post.

entries.name: Ammi
entries.note: Hosea 2:1 uses a meaningful designation; Hitchcock's cross-reference to Ammah is unsubstantiated here.

strongs.strongs_def: a people (as a congregated unit); specifically, a tribe (as those of Israel); hence (collectively) troops or attendants; figuratively, a flock

entries.name: Ammi-nadab
entries.note: H5992 supports this lexical sense, but Ammi-nadab has no supplied KJV reference; retain spelling identification as provisional. [Strong H5992](https://biblehub.com/hebrew/5992.htm).

strongs.derivation: from H5971 (עַם) and H5068 (נָדַב); people of liberality;
strongs.strongs_def: Amminadab, the name of four Israelites

entries.name: Ammiel
entries.note: Strong H5988 proposes this sense; Hitchcock: the people of God. These are secondary lexical claims, not the biblical text.

strongs.derivation: from H5971 (עַם) and H410 (אֵל); people of God;
strongs.strongs_def: Ammiel, the name of three or four Israelites

entries.name: Ammihud
entries.displayMeaning: People of splendor; variant: people of nobility
entries.note: H5989 and H5991 represent distinct forms/identities, not one interchangeable definition.

strongs.derivation: from H5971 (עַם) and H1935 (הוֹד); people of splendor;
strongs.strongs_def: Ammihud, the name of three Israelites

strongs.derivation: from H5971 (עַם) and H2353 (חוּר); people of nobility;

entries.name: Ammishaddai
entries.note: H5996 supports the first phrase, not the Almighty is with me. [Strong H5996](https://biblehub.com/hebrew/5996.htm).
hitchcock: the people of the Almighty; the Almighty is with me

strongs.derivation: from H5971 (עַם) and H7706 (שַׁדַּי); people of (the) Almighty;

entries.name: Ammizabad
entries.note: Strong H5990 proposes this sense; Hitchcock: dowry of the people. These are secondary lexical claims, not the biblical text.

strongs.derivation: from H5971 (עַם) and H2064 (זָבַד); people of endowment;

entries.name: Ammon
entries.note: H5983 concerns Lot's son, his descendants and their territory; distinguish those uses.
hitchcock: a people; the son of my people

strongs.strongs_def: Ammon, a son of Lot; also his posterity and their country

entries.name: Amnon
entries.note: H550 does not give tutor. [Strong H550](https://biblehub.com/hebrew/550.htm).

strongs.strongs_def: Amnon (or Aminon), a son of David

entries.name: Amok
entries.note: Strong H5987 proposes this sense; Hitchcock: a valley; a depth. These are secondary lexical claims, not the biblical text.

entries.name: Amon
entries.note: H526 refers to H525 (skilled/architect); faithful/true is not the supplied name derivation.

strongs.strongs_def: Amon, the name of three Israelites

strongs.derivation: from H539 (אָמַן), probably in the sense of training; like H542 (אָמָן)

entries.name: Amorite
entries.note: H567 gives a tentative derivation from prominence; bitter/rebel/babbler is a different proposal. This is a people-name. [Strong H567](https://biblehub.com/hebrew/567.htm).

strongs.derivation: probably a patronymic from an unused name derived from H559 (אָמַר) in the sense of publicity, i.e. prominence; thus, a mountaineer;
strongs.strongs_def: an Emorite, one of the Canaanitish tribes

entries.name: Amos
entries.note: Amos the prophet (Amos 1:1, H5986) differs from the genealogical Amos (Luke 3:25, G301), whom Strong derives from Amoz H531, strong. Do not merge their etymologies.

entries.name: Amoz
entries.note: The compared sources broadly agree on this core sense; this is a lexical proposal, not an assertion about character.

entries.name: Amplias
entries.note: The pinned Strong G291 record supplies this lexical proposal, compatible with Hitchcock's core sense. This dictionary comparison does not establish the etymology as biblical fact. [Strong G291](https://biblehub.com/greek/291.htm).

entries.name: Amram
entries.note: Strong supports exalted people, with probable derivation; sheaves and handfuls are unestablished alternatives.
hitchcock: an exalted people; their sheaves; handfuls of corn

strongs.derivation: probably from H5971 (עַם) and H7311 (רוּם); high people;
strongs.strongs_def: Amram, the name of two Israelites

entries.name: Amraphel
entries.note: The supplied Strong entry differs from Hitchcock or leaves the derivation unresolved; retain source attribution.

entries.name: Amzi
entries.note: The pinned Strong H557 record supplies this lexical proposal, compatible with Hitchcock's core sense. This dictionary comparison does not establish the etymology as biblical fact. [Strong H557](https://biblehub.com/hebrew/557.htm).

entries.name: Anab
entries.note: Strong H6024 proposes this sense; Hitchcock: a grape; a knot. These are secondary lexical claims, not the biblical text.

strongs.derivation: from the same as H6025 (עֵנָב); fruit;

entries.name: Anah
entries.note: H6034 gives a probable derivation, not a certain second sense afflicted.

strongs.strongs_def: Anah, the name of two Edomites and one Edomitess

entries.name: Anaharath
entries.note: H588 differs from dryness, burning and wrath. [Strong H588](https://biblehub.com/hebrew/588.htm).

strongs.derivation: probably from the same root as H5170 (נַחַר); a gorge or narrow pass;

entries.name: Anak
entries.note: Strong H6061, H6060 proposes this sense; Hitchcock: a collar; ornament. These are secondary lexical claims, not the biblical text.

entries.name: Anamim
entries.note: The supplied Strong entry differs from Hitchcock or leaves the derivation unresolved; retain source attribution.

strongs.derivation: as if plural of some Egyptian word;
strongs.strongs_def: Anamim, a son of Mizraim and his descendants, with their country

entries.name: Anammelech
entries.note: H6048 supplies foreign origin; Hebrew answer/poverty of king is unestablished. [Strong H6048](https://biblehub.com/hebrew/6048.htm).

entries.name: Anani
entries.note: Cloud is supported; prophecy and divination are not established by Strong's cloud derivation.

entries.name: Ananias
entries.note: G367 points to Hananiah H2608; cloud of the Lord belongs to a different analysis.
hitchcock: or Ananiah, the cloud of the Lord

strongs.strongs_def: Ananias, the name of three Israelites

strongs.derivation: or חֲנַנְיָהוּ; from H2603 (חָנַן) and H3050 (יָהּ); Jah has favored;
strongs.strongs_def: Chananjah, the name of thirteen Israelites

entries.name: Anathema
entries.displayMeaning: religious ban; accursed thing or person
entries.note: G331 is a common term in 1 Corinthians 16:22, not a person's name; separated understates the sense. [Strong G331](https://biblehub.com/greek/331.htm).

strongs.strongs_def: a (religious) ban or (concretely) excommunicated (thing or person)

entries.name: Anathoth
entries.note: Strong derives Anathoth from Anath, answer. Song and poverty are not established; the spelling covers a place and persons.

strongs.strongs_def: Anathoth, the name of two Israelites, also of a place in Pal

entries.name: Andrew
entries.note: The compared sources broadly agree on this core sense; this is a lexical proposal, not an assertion about character.

entries.name: Andronicus
entries.note: G408's kjv_def is digitally misspelled Adronicus; its lemma/transliteration identify Andronicus, Romans 16:7. [Strong G408](https://biblehub.com/greek/408.htm).

strongs.strongs_def: man of victory; Andronicos, an Israelite

entries.name: Anem
entries.note: Strong H6046 proposes this sense; Hitchcock: or Anen, an answer; their affliction. These are secondary lexical claims, not the biblical text.
hitchcock: or Anen, an answer; their affliction

strongs.derivation: from the dual of H5869 (עַיִן); two fountains;

entries.name: Aner
entries.note: H6063 probably relates the name to H5288; the Hitchcock meanings are unsupported by that proposal.

strongs.strongs_def: Aner, a Amorite, also a place in Palestine

entries.name: Aniam
entries.note: H593 supports sorrow but not strength. [Strong H593](https://biblehub.com/hebrew/593.htm).
hitchcock: a people; the strength or sorrow of people

strongs.derivation: from H578 (אָנָה) and H5971 (עַם); groaning of (the) people;

entries.name: Anim
entries.note: Strong H6044 proposes this sense; Hitchcock: answerings; singings; afflicted. These are secondary lexical claims, not the biblical text.

entries.name: Anna
entries.note: G451 points to Hannah H2584; gracious broadly agrees, but one who gives is not a distinct established derivation.

entries.name: Annas
entries.note: G452 links to H2608 Hananiah; answers/humble is not the cited Hebrew derivation. [Strong G452](https://biblehub.com/greek/452.htm).

entries.name: Antichrist
entries.note: G500 is the noun rendered antichrist in 1 John 2:18,22; it is a designation, not an ordinary personal proper name. Do not use the incidental Gog entry G1136 as the lexical match.

entries.name: Antioch
entries.note: G490 derives the city name from a Syrian king; speedy as a chariot is not supplied. Multiple cities require contextual identification.

entries.name: Antipas
entries.displayMeaning: name formed from against/instead of and father
entries.note: G493 refers to father, not all; the contracted name's full interpretation remains cautious. [Strong G493](https://biblehub.com/greek/493.htm).

strongs.derivation: contracted for a compound of G473 (ἀντί) and a derivative of G3962 (πατήρ);

entries.name: Antipatris
entries.note: Strong derives the place from the same compound as Antipas; it does not establish both for and against as interchangeable meanings.

strongs.derivation: contracted for a compound of G473 (ἀντί) and a derivative of G3962 (πατήρ);

entries.name: Antothijah
entries.note: Answers agrees; songs and afflictions are not independently established by H6070.
hitchcock: answers or songs of the Lord; afflictions

strongs.derivation: from the same as H6068 (עֲנָתוֹת) and H3050 (יָהּ); answers of Jah;

entries.name: Anub
entries.note: H6036 does not identify Anub with Anab; a cross-reference alone obscures the different forms. [Strong H6036](https://biblehub.com/hebrew/6036.htm).

strongs.derivation: passive participle from the same as H6025 (עֵנָב); borne (as fruit);

entries.name: Apelles
entries.note: Strong G559 proposes this sense; Hitchcock: exclusion; separation. The derivation remains uncertain.

entries.name: Apharsathchites
entries.note: H671 identifies an unknown Assyrian tribe and contains the digital KJV variant Apharasthchites; dividing/rending is not supplied.
hitchcock: Apharsites (from a root meaning) dividing or rending

strongs.derivation: (Aramaic) or אֲפַרְסַתְכַי; (Aramaic), of foreign origin (only in the plural);
strongs.strongs_def: an Apharsekite or Apharsathkite, an unknown Assyrian tribe

entries.name: Aphek

hitchcock: Aphekah, Aphik, strength; a rapid torrent

strongs.derivation: or אֲפִיק; from H662 (אָפַק) (in the sense of strength); fortress;
strongs.strongs_def: Aphek (or Aphik), the name of three places in Palestine

entries.name: Aphiah
entries.note: Strong H647 proposes this sense; Hitchcock: speaking, blowing. These are secondary lexical claims, not the biblical text.

entries.name: Apocalypse
entries.note: Book-title term rather than a KJV personal/place name; no KJV occurrence supplied.

entries.name: Apocrypha
entries.note: No supplied KJV verse identifies Apocrypha as a biblical person or place; distinguish a category of writings from a Bible name.

entries.name: Apollonia
entries.note: G624 associates the place with the pagan deity. Its proposed connection with destroy does not make perdition the entire place-name meaning.

strongs.derivation: from the pagan deity (i.e. the sun;
strongs.strongs_def: from G622 (ἀπόλλυμι)); Apollonia, a place in Macedonia

entries.name: Apollonius
entries.note: No exact candidate or KJV reference supplied; canonical membership unresolved.

entries.name: Apollos
entries.displayMeaning: name associated with Apollonia/Apollo; precise derivation unresolved
entries.note: G625 says probably from G624 Apollonia. The destroying gloss is not established by that entry. [Strong G625](https://biblehub.com/greek/625.htm).

strongs.derivation: probably from the same as G624 (Ἀπολλωνία);

entries.name: Apollyon
entries.note: Revelation 9:11 expressly pairs Apollyon with Abaddon as the angel of the bottomless pit; Strong's parenthetical Satan is commentary, not wording of that verse.

entries.name: Appaim
entries.note: The compared sources broadly agree on this core sense; this is a lexical proposal, not an assertion about character.

entries.name: Apphia
entries.note: G682 does not establish productive or fruitful. [Strong G682](https://biblehub.com/greek/682.htm).

entries.name: Aquila
entries.note: Strong G207 proposes this sense; Hitchcock: an eagle. These are secondary lexical claims, not the biblical text.

entries.name: Ar
entries.note: The supplied Strong entry differs from Hitchcock or leaves the derivation unresolved; retain source attribution.

entries.name: Arab
entries.note: Strong H694 proposes this sense; Hitchcock: multiplying; sowing sedition; a window; a locust. These are secondary lexical claims, not the biblical text.
hitchcock: multiplying; sowing sedition; a window; a locust

entries.name: Arabia
entries.note: H6152 gives an aridity/sterility derivation; H6154 is a common noun for mixture/weaving, not a second proper-name derivation. Evening and ravens are not established.

strongs.strongs_def: Arab (i.e. Arabia), a country East of Palestine

strongs.derivation: or עֶרֶב; (1 Kings 10:15), (with the article [prefix), from H6148 (עָרַב);
strongs.strongs_def: the web (or transverse threads of cloth); also a mixture, (or mongrel race)

strongs.strongs_def: Arad, the name of a place near Palestine, also of a Canaanite and an Israelite

entries.name: Arah
entries.note: Strong H733 proposes this sense; Hitchcock: the way; a traveler. These are secondary lexical claims, not the biblical text.

strongs.strongs_def: Arach, the name of three Israelites

entries.name: Aram

strongs.derivation: from the same as H759 (אַרְמוֹן); the highland;
strongs.strongs_def: Aram or Syria, and its inhabitants; also the name of the son of Shem, a grandson of Nahor, and of an Israelite

entries.name: Aran
entries.note: H765 differs from ark/curse. [Strong H765](https://biblehub.com/hebrew/765.htm).

entries.name: Ararat
entries.note: Strong H780 proposes this sense; Hitchcock: the curse of trembling. The derivation remains uncertain.

entries.name: Araunah
entries.note: H728 points to Ornan H771, which proposes strong only probably; ark/song/joyful cry is not supported.

entries.name: Arba

entries.name: Archelaus
entries.note: The lexical sense agrees with Hitchcock; the transcription's G2994 link is Laodiceus, not an independent proof of the people element. Flag that digital cross-reference for review.

entries.name: Archippus
entries.note: The compared sources broadly agree on this core sense; this is a lexical proposal, not an assertion about character.

entries.name: Arcturus

strongs.strongs_def: Ard, the name of two Israelites

entries.name: Ardon

strongs.derivation: from the same as H714 (אַרְדְּ); roaming;

hitchcock: the light or vision of God

entries.name: Areopagus

entries.name: Aretas
entries.note: The supplied Strong entry differs from Hitchcock or leaves the derivation unresolved; retain source attribution.

entries.name: Argob
entries.note: H709 differs from turf/fat land. [Strong H709](https://biblehub.com/hebrew/709.htm).

strongs.derivation: from the same as H7263 (רֶגֶב); stony;

entries.name: Ariel

strongs.strongs_def: Ariel, a symbolical name for Jerusalem, also the name of an Israelite

strongs.derivation: or אֲרִאֵל; from H738 (אֲרִי) and H410 (אֵל);

entries.note: H746 does not establish long/great/tall. [Strong H746](https://biblehub.com/hebrew/746.htm).

strongs.strongs_def: Arjok, the name of two Babylonians

strongs.derivation: from the same as G712 (ἄριστον) and G1012 (βουλή);

hitchcock: hill of fruits; mountain of Megiddo

entries.name: Arnon

entries.name: Aroer

entries.name: Arpad
entries.note: H774 differs from light of redemption. [Strong H774](https://biblehub.com/hebrew/774.htm).

strongs.derivation: contracted from a compound of G735 (Ἄρτεμις) and G1435 (δῶρον);

entries.name: Arumah

strongs.strongs_def: Asa, the name of a king and of a Levite

strongs.strongs_def: Asajah, the name of three or four Israelites

entries.name: Asaph
entries.note: The compared sources broadly agree on this core sense; this is a lexical proposal, not an assertion about character.

strongs.strongs_def: Asaph, the name of three Israelites, and of the family of the first

entries.name: Asenath

entries.name: Ashan
entries.note: H6228 points to H6227 for the common noun smoke.

strongs.derivation: probably from the same as H7640 (שֹׁבֶל); flowing;

entries.note: H807 does not establish crime/offense. [Strong H807](https://biblehub.com/hebrew/807.htm).

strongs.strongs_def: Ashkenaz, a Japhethite, also his descendants

entries.name: Bartholomew

entries.name: Bartimeus
entries.displayMeaning: meaning not established for this spelling
entries.note: No exact candidate or supplied KJV reference for Bartimeus. G924 identifies Bartimaeus; its alternative unclean conflicts with honorable and requires a separately evidenced spelling link.

entries.name: Baruch
entries.note: Strong H1263 proposes this sense; Hitchcock: who is blessed. These are secondary lexical claims, not the biblical text.

strongs.strongs_def: Baruk, the name of three Israelites

entries.name: Barzillai

hitchcock: son of contempt; made of iron

strongs.strongs_def: Barzillai, the name of three Israelites

entries.name: Bashan
entries.note: H1316 explicitly marks derivation uncertain. [Strong H1316](https://biblehub.com/hebrew/1316.htm).

strongs.strongs_def: Bashan (often with the article), a region East of the Jordan

entries.name: Bashemath

hitchcock: perfumed; confusion of death; in desolation

strongs.derivation: feminine of H1314 (בֶּשֶׂם) (the second form); fragrance;
strongs.strongs_def: Bosmath, the name of a wife of Esau, and of a daughter of Solomon

entries.name: Bathsuha
entries.displayMeaning: meaning not established for this spelling
entries.note: Bathsuha has no supplied reference. H1340 Bath-shua is equated with Bathsheba, but the spelling requires confirmation rather than silent normalization.

entries.name: Bealiah
entries.note: Strong H1183 proposes this sense; Hitchcock: the god of an idol; in an assembly. These are secondary lexical claims, not the biblical text.

strongs.derivation: from H1167 (בַּעַל) and H3050 (יָהּ); Jah (is) master;

entries.name: Bealoth
entries.note: Strong differs from Hitchcock or explicitly leaves derivation unresolved; neither proposal is thereby proved.

strongs.kjv_def: Bealoth, in Aloth (by mistake for a plural from H5927 (עָלָה) with prepositional prefix).

entries.name: Bebai
entries.displayMeaning: probably foreign name; meaning not supplied
entries.note: H893 does not establish void/empty. [Strong H893](https://biblehub.com/hebrew/893.htm).

entries.name: Becher
entries.note: H1071 links the name to H1070, a young camel; firstborn is a competing derivation.

strongs.strongs_def: Beker, the name of two Israelites

strongs.derivation: from H1069 (בָּכַר) (in the sense of youth);

entries.name: Bechorath
entries.note: H1064 concerns firstborn status, not agricultural first fruits.

entries.name: Bedad
entries.note: The pinned Strong H911 record supplies this lexical proposal, compatible with Hitchcock's core sense. This dictionary comparison does not establish the etymology as biblical fact. [Strong H911](https://biblehub.com/hebrew/911.htm).

entries.name: Bedaiah
entries.note: The alternative spelling Bedeiah corresponds to H912 (Ezra 10:35); its proposed servant of Jehovah differs from only Lord.

strongs.derivation: probably a shortened form H5662 (עֹבַדְיָה); servant of Jehovah;

entries.name: Bedan
entries.note: H917's shortening from Abdon is explicitly probable; judgment is unsupported.

strongs.strongs_def: Bedan, the name of two Israelites

entries.name: Beeliada
entries.note: H1182 differs from open idol. [Strong H1182](https://biblehub.com/hebrew/1182.htm).

strongs.derivation: from H1168 (בַּעַל) and H3045 (יָדַע); Baal has known;

entries.name: Beelzebub
entries.note: Strong calls this a parody on Baal-zebub H1176. Preserve that as Strong's attributed explanation, not an unqualified offensive replacement or a claim that both spellings have identical senses.

strongs.strongs_def: dung-god; Beelzebul, a name of Satan
strongs.derivation: of Chaldee origin (by parody on H01176);

entries.name: Beer
entries.note: The compared sources broadly agree on this core lexical proposal.

strongs.strongs_def: Beer, a place in the Desert, also one in Palestine

entries.name: Beer-lahai-roi

entries.name: Beera
entries.note: Well is supported; declaring is not established.

strongs.derivation: from H875 (בְּאֵר) and the plural of H410 (אֵל); well of heroes;
strongs.strongs_def: Beer-Elim, a place in the Desert

entries.name: Beeri

strongs.strongs_def: Beeri, the name of a Hittite and of an Israelite

entries.name: Beeroth
entries.note: Wells is supported; explaining is not established.

strongs.derivation: from H875 (בְּאֵר) and H7651 (שֶׁבַע) (in the sense of H7650 (שָׁבַע)); well of an oath;

entries.name: Bekah

entries.name: Belah

strongs.strongs_def: Bela, the name of a place, also of an Edomite and of two Israelites

strongs.kjv_def: devouring, that which he hath swallowed up.

entries.name: Belial
entries.note: H1100 is a Hebrew moral term in sons of Belial; G955 is an epithet of Satan in 2 Corinthians 6:15. Do not treat every Old Testament occurrence as a personal name. [Strong H1100](https://biblehub.com/hebrew/1100.htm); [Strong G955](https://biblehub.com/greek/955.htm).

worthlessness; Belial, as an epithet of Satan

entries.name: Belshazzar

entries.name: Belteshazzar
